hero.headline: Anthropic Raises $65 Billion, Surpassing OpenAI's Valuation
hero.body:
Anthropic has completed a Series H funding round raising $65 billion at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, making it the world's most valuable AI startup and surpassing its rival OpenAI. The funding round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital.

The valuation represents a dramatic shift in the competitive landscape of the AI industry. Anthropic, which once occupied a smaller position in the global AI race, has emerged as a dominant player through widespread enterprise adoption of its products. The company's Claude chatbot and powerful coding assistants released last year have driven much of this growth and commercial prominence.

Krishna Rao, Anthropic's chief financial officer, highlighted the company's momentum in a statement: "Claude is increasingly indispensable to our growing global community of customers, and we work tirelessly to make tools like Claude Code and Cowork more helpful, more powerful, and more adaptable to their needs."

The company has distinguished itself through an enterprise-focused business strategy and a public commitment to AI safety. Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah appeared at the Vatican for Pope Leo XIV's release of a major encyclical warning about artificial intelligence's dangers and calling for stronger oversight of the technology. The company has also refused to remove safeguards from Claude that would allow its use in mass domestic surveillance or lethal autonomous weapons systems, leading to a legal dispute with the Pentagon.

Beyond product development, Anthropic has positioned itself as a proponent of government regulation in the AI space, diverging from other tech industry leaders. The company has invested millions in lobbying efforts and Super PACs supporting candidates and legislation aligned with its regulatory vision.

This valuation milestone underscores the substantial capital continuing to flow into the AI sector despite public concerns about the technology. The funding provides Anthropic with resources to further develop its AI systems and compete against OpenAI and other rivals in the rapidly expanding market.

The timing has broader implications for the technology industry. OpenAI raised $122 billion in March to reach a valuation of $852 billion and is expected to pursue a potential trillion-dollar initial public offering later this year. Anthropic's latest success adds to what is shaping up to be a blockbuster year for IPOs among AI companies and their competitors.

The deal reflects how intensely investors continue to back AI development despite questions about long-term profitability and business model sustainability. As both Anthropic and OpenAI race to develop and commercialize advanced language models and related technologies, valuations in the sector have climbed sharply.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.body:
President Trump asked for several amendments to a nuclear agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to administration officials and sources briefed on the discussions.

Trump wants to finalize the deal soon but is seeking to strengthen several points that matter to him, particularly regarding Iran's nuclear material, two U.S. officials said. The president expects to complete the agreement despite the requested changes.

Trump's request has launched another round of negotiations between the parties that could last several more days. The back-and-forth comes as the administration works to extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The two sides reached a tentative agreement earlier in the week. If both Trump and Tehran ultimately approve the final terms, the emerging deal would mark a significant shift in U.S.-Iran relations. Details of a potential agreement include that the strait would reopen with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, while Iran would be able to freely sell oil. According to reports, negotiations would be held on curbing Iran's nuclear program. In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports.

Trump announced on Saturday that a peace deal "has been largely negotiated," after calls with a Pakistani mediator and Gulf allies. He wrote on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" were still being discussed and "will be announced shortly."

However, Iran's Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, reported that the strait of Hormuz would remain under Iranian control. The news agency stated that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

Pakistan's prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the U.S. and Iran "very soon." Pakistan's army chief, Syed Asim Munir, is a key figure in the negotiations.

The amendments focus on specific provisions related to Iran's nuclear program. Trump's decision to request modifications indicates his personal involvement in the final stages of the diplomatic process.

The agreement remains unsigned as the administration works to address Trump's concerns about nuclear material provisions and other key elements. Trump has said he would only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," adding that if an agreement was not reached, the U.S. would begin striking Iran again.

The negotiations have sparked criticism from Republican hawks who have spent years calling for military action against Iran and opposing the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated during the Obama administration.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch significant attacks within the next two days based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a major Russian attack expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence assessments from the U.S. and European allies. He anticipates the offensive will occur at night and involve significant Russian military forces.

The warning reflects ongoing concerns about Russian military operations against Ukraine and the coordination between Zelensky's government and Western intelligence partners in monitoring potential threats.

cards.headline: Israeli Soldiers Describe Ongoing Killings in Gaza Despite Ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers shared accounts describing continued killings in Gaza even after a ceasefire was announced.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers provided rare firsthand accounts to reporters describing ongoing military operations and killings in Gaza following the announcement of a ceasefire. One soldier said calling it a ceasefire was inaccurate given the continuing violence.

An Israeli commander told reporters that Hezbollah had planned attacks on Israel similar to those carried out by Hamas. The soldiers' accounts offer a window into military operations that continue despite official ceasefire declarations.

cards.headline: China's Factory Activity Declines Further
cards.teaser: Manufacturing indicators show continued weakness in China's industrial sector.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China has weakened, signaling concerns about the world's second-largest economy. The decline in manufacturing indicators reflects broader challenges facing China's industrial sector, which has historically been central to the country's economic growth.

Sustained weakness in manufacturing could have ripple effects on global supply chains and trade patterns worldwide. Policymakers are closely monitoring these economic indicators as they assess the health of China's economy and its implications for international commerce.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Kills More Than 245 as Aid Agencies Rush to Help
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed at least 65 confirmed deaths, with 246 suspected cases reported so far, according to health officials. The virus has primarily affected Ituri province, a conflict-hit region that shares borders with Uganda and South Sudan. Uganda's health ministry confirmed its own outbreak, reporting that a 59-year-old man died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The World Health Organization has estimated the death rate between 30 and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. "It's huge. It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die," said Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team. The WHO's director visited the worst-hit areas to support containment efforts.

Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières described the situation as deeply alarming, warning that the virus is spreading rapidly through communities with limited medical infrastructure. Health workers in affected regions lack adequate equipment and trained personnel to contain the outbreak and implement standard containment measures such as contact tracing and isolation.

The strain identified in testing samples is Bundibugyo Ebola, for which no licensed vaccine exists. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed the virus was detected in 13 of 20 samples tested. This strain has appeared only twice before, in 2007 and 2012.

Ituri province presents particular challenges for disease control. As a major mining hub, the region experiences constant movement of workers and high population density in close quarters. The area is also affected by ongoing conflict between armed groups, forcing waves of displaced people into overcrowded camps. These conditions create ideal circumstances for rapid virus transmission while making coordination of public health responses extremely difficult.

Officials from the Africa CDC, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, South Sudan, and the WHO convened an urgent meeting to coordinate regional response efforts. "Given the high population movement between affected areas and neighbouring countries, rapid regional coordination is essential," said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of Africa CDC.

Aid organizations are working to deliver supplies and personnel to affected regions to support local health workers. However, the underdeveloped health infrastructure across much of the country continues to complicate these efforts. Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in neighboring Bunia.

The Democratic Republic of Congo has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976. This current outbreak represents another serious health crisis for a nation repeatedly vulnerable to infectious disease spread due to geographic, environmental, and socioeconomic factors.

cards.headline: Eleven dead after chemical tank explosion at Washington paper mill
cards.body:
Authorities recovered and identified all eleven victims of a chemical tank explosion at a Nippon paper mill in Longview, Washington. The incident involved a tank implosion at the facility.

Officials initially reported nine people missing after the explosion. Search and recovery efforts have now concluded with all victims accounted for.

The explosion occurred at the industrial paper manufacturing facility operated by Nippon. Longview officials coordinated the recovery operation to locate those who were missing following the blast.

Authorities have identified all eleven people killed in the incident. The tank implosion caused the fatalities at the mill site.

The cause of the chemical tank explosion has not been detailed in available reports. The incident represents one of the larger industrial accidents in recent months.

Paper mills process wood pulp and other materials using various chemicals and industrial equipment. The Longview facility is part of Nippon's manufacturing operations.

Recovery teams worked to locate all missing individuals after the initial explosion. The operation moved through several stages as officials worked to account for everyone at the site when the incident occurred.

The eleven confirmed deaths mark the total loss of life from the industrial accident. All victims have been recovered from the scene and identified by authorities.

Longview officials oversaw the response to the tank implosion. The incident required coordination among multiple agencies to conduct the search and recovery operation.

The explosion at the Nippon mill facility drew attention to safety protocols at industrial chemical sites. The tank implosion created conditions that required extensive recovery efforts by emergency personnel.

cards.headline: Five Freed From Flooded Cave in Laos After More Than a Week Trapped
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed five people from a flooded cave in Laos after they were trapped for over a week.
cards.body:
Rescuers have freed five of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for 10 days. The miners had entered the narrow tunnels on May 20 in search of gold when they became trapped. The first person was rescued on Friday, followed by four more men in a hazardous operation that required teams to drain water from the cave and navigate collapse hazards.

Two villagers remain missing as divers continue searching through the flooded tunnels. The rescue mission has involved navigating muddy water and sharp rocks deep within the cave system to locate the trapped individuals.

cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers shared accounts describing continued killings in Gaza even after a ceasefire was announced.

An Israeli commander told reporters that Hezbollah had planned attacks on Israel similar to those carried out by Hamas. The soldiers' accounts offer a window into military operations that continue despite official ceasefire declarations.

cards.headline: Hundreds Arrested in France After Champions League Celebrations Turn Violent
cards.teaser: French police arrested hundreds of people after celebrations of PSG's Champions League victory led to clashes.
cards.body:
More than 280 people were arrested in Paris following PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal. Thousands of police officers were deployed across the city as celebrations turned violent, with some fans firing flares and clashing with authorities.

The unrest caught officials off guard despite expectations of large crowds gathering to celebrate PSG retaining their Champions League title. Police worked to manage the disorder as fans became unruly throughout Paris.

cards.headline: Japan Rejects China's Accusations of New Militarism
cards.teaser: Japan's defense minister rejected Chinese claims of new militarism and pointed to China's own military expansion.
cards.body:
Japan's defence minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected Chinese accusations of new militarism, asserting that Japan remains a peace-loving nation. He criticized China for expanding its military capabilities without sufficient transparency, raising regional security concerns.

Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's leadership, Japan has accelerated its shift toward a more proactive defence policy, moving away from the pacifist stance adopted after World War II. This strategic reorientation has been encouraged by the United States as Japan continues strengthening its military capabilities.

cards.headline: Drone Crashes Into Romanian Apartment Building as War Affects Civilian Areas
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war close to civilian homes.
cards.body:
A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania early Friday morning, sparking a fire and forcing residents to evacuate. People have only just begun returning to check on their homes in the damaged block.

The incident underscores the dangers facing civilians in Romania, which shares a border with Ukraine and lies in close proximity to the Russia-Ukraine war. Residents expressed deep anxiety about their safety, with some saying they no longer feel secure in their own homes.

cards.headline: Taiwan Debates Infiltration Concerns After Chinese-Born Woman Accused
cards.teaser: An infiltration case involving a Chinese-born woman has sparked debate in Taiwan over security measures and profiling.
cards.body:
Taiwan is grappling with questions about how to defend against infiltration without profiling migrants from mainland China after authorities accused a Chinese-born woman of infiltration activities. The case has become a focal point for discussions about security and civil liberties.

Thousands of people from mainland China live in Taiwan after marrying Taiwanese citizens. The case has raised concerns about balancing national security with fair treatment of this population.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran nuclear framework negotiated by envoys
cards.teaser: The president asked for edits to the Iran agreement his envoys had negotiated.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his cabinet to make a final determination on an Iran nuclear deal framework that US and Iranian officials had agreed upon. Rather than announcing a deal, Trump requested modifications to the agreement, sending tougher terms to Iran for consideration.

Defense Secretary Hegseth discussed the ongoing negotiations as the administration continues to weigh its position on the framework.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump plan to add name to Kennedy Center and halt renovation
cards.teaser: A federal judge blocked the president's Kennedy Center plans, preventing the addition of his name to the venue.
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked President Trump's plans for the Kennedy Center, preventing a proposed closure and stopping the administration from adding Trump's name to the Washington performing arts venue. The ruling halted the intended renovation changes to the institution.

The decision has drawn criticism from Trump, who expressed frustration over the legal setback and disputed the judge's ruling.

cards.headline: Family of four among five killed in Virginia bus crash on way to wedding
cards.teaser: A crash in Virginia killed five people, including a family of four traveling to a wedding.
cards.body:
Five people died in a crash in Virginia, including a family of four who were traveling to attend a wedding. Authorities charged the bus driver in connection with the incident.

The crash involved a bus and resulted in multiple fatalities. The family of four was among those killed in the collision.

cards.headline: Four inmates escape Alabama correctional facility
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for four Alabama inmates who escaped from a correctional center.
cards.body:
Four inmates escaped from an Alabama correctional center, prompting a search by authorities. The escape occurred at a facility in the state.

Officials launched a search operation to locate the four escapees. The inmates remain at large following their escape from the correctional center.

cards.headline: Meteor explosion over Massachusetts causes loud booms across New England
cards.teaser: A meteor exploded over Massachusetts, creating loud booms heard throughout southern New England.
cards.body:
A meteor traveling at 75,000 miles per hour exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The fireball broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles, generating loud booms that echoed across the region.

The explosion prompted widespread reports throughout southern New England, with the sound heard by hundreds of residents across multiple states.

cards.headline: Becerra leads California governor race in latest polling
cards.teaser: Xavier Becerra gained support in recent polling for California governor, with Tom Steyer and Steve Hilton trailing.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra is leading in the California governor race as the state heads toward its June 2 primary election. The Democratic candidate is locked in a tight three-way contest with fellow Democrat Tom Steyer and Republican Steve Hilton.

Voters are heading into Tuesday's primary with frustration and disappointment, with little clarity emerging in the final stretch of the campaign. Beyond the governor's race, Californians will also decide a competitive Los Angeles mayoral contest and several congressional races that could influence control of the US House in November.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans Up to $75 Billion Investment in French AI Data Centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate announces what would be Europe's largest AI facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, establishing what would be Europe's largest AI facility. Founder Masayoshi Son announced the commitment, positioning France as a major hub for AI infrastructure development in Europe.

The investment will develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity, providing the computing power needed to develop and run AI systems across the continent.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Receives National Security Contract Hours Before Rocket Explosion
cards.teaser: The company secured a defense task order shortly before an explosion at its Florida launch site.
cards.body:
Blue Origin received a national security launch task order hours before a New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad on Thursday night at 9pm ET, with the orange glow visible over 100 miles away in Fort Pierce.

No personnel were harmed in the incident, which the company described as an anomaly. Blue Origin has since regained access to Launch Complex 36. The explosion threatens NASA's lunar base plans and its goal to return humans to the moon within two years.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts Cockpit Breach
cards.teaser: A man allegedly tried to enter the cockpit of a Chicago-to-Minneapolis flight, forcing an emergency landing.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after a passenger allegedly attempted to breach the cockpit. Flight 2005 made an emergency landing in Madison, Wisconsin, where the man was arrested. The incident triggered a hijacking alert.

The FBI has not yet filed criminal charges following the emergency landing and arrest. Authorities detained the passenger after crew members and other passengers reportedly subdued him during the attempted cockpit intrusion.

cards.headline: U.S. New Car Buyers Drop by One Million
cards.teaser: Auto sales have declined for eight consecutive months as fewer Americans purchase vehicles.
cards.body:
The U.S. new car market has shed one million buyers, with sales declining for eight consecutive months. The decline stems from weakening demand for electric vehicles and financial strain on consumers.

Despite the sales slump, automakers have maintained profitability through pricing strategies and cost management. The shrinking buyer pool indicates that new car ownership is becoming less accessible for many Americans.

cards.headline: China's Biotechnology Industry Gains Ground on U.S. Dominance
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are drawing attention at a major oncology conference.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted in China are receiving attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago. This visibility reflects China's rapidly expanding biotechnology and pharmaceutical research sector, which has prompted concern about the erosion of American leadership in drug development.

Chinese companies and research institutions are making substantial investments in medical research and development, strengthening the country's competitive position in the global biotechnology market.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, causing loud booms heard across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a powerful blast that was heard and felt across a wide region. The explosion occurred just after 2pm local time, according to Nasa officials.

The fireball broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour. The blast was equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, producing sonic booms that resonated across New England and beyond. Hundreds of residents reported hearing and feeling the explosion, which left many puzzled about its source before authorities confirmed the meteor explanation.

Reports of the event came from a wide geographic area. Sightings extended from Delaware to Montreal, demonstrating how far the sound waves traveled from the explosion site. The widespread nature of the reports suggests the meteor was at a significant altitude when it broke apart, allowing the shock waves to reach populated areas across multiple states and into Canada.

Residents who experienced the boom described it as mysterious and startling. Many turned to social media and contacted local authorities to report the strange noise before the cause became clear. People in the Boston area and surrounding regions were particularly affected by the explosion.

When a meteor enters Earth's atmosphere at high speed, it generates intense heat. This causes rapid expansion of gases and creates a shock wave that produces the characteristic loud boom. A sonic boom occurs when an object travels through the atmosphere faster than the speed of sound, compressing the air in front of it and creating a pressure wave.

While meteors regularly enter Earth's atmosphere, most burn up completely without creating noticeable sounds or visual displays. The ones that explode with enough force to generate sonic booms are considerably less common and typically attract significant public attention when they occur over populated areas.

This event illustrates how even relatively small space rocks can produce dramatic effects when they enter the atmosphere at extreme velocities. The explosion over Massachusetts was detected by multiple monitoring systems and confirmed by Nasa officials.

The agency's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren provided confirmation of the event to news organizations. Nasa continues to track and study such incidents as part of its efforts to monitor near-Earth objects and understand meteorite impacts on the planet.

The loud booms and the resulting public reports highlight how visible and audible such celestial events can be, even when occurring high in the atmosphere. For residents across New England, the mysterious sound served as a reminder of the dynamic processes occurring in the skies above Earth.

cards.headline: Nvidia-powered Windows PCs to debut next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers using Nvidia processors instead of traditional Intel or AMD chips will be unveiled at an upcoming event.
cards.body:
Microsoft and Nvidia are preparing to introduce the first Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips at an event next week, according to Axios. The new processors, called N1X, represent a shift from the Intel and AMD chips that have traditionally powered Windows computers.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and chip designer Arm have all posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the GTC event. The new Arm-powered Windows PC chips would mark Nvidia's entry into the laptop processor market, potentially reshaping the competitive landscape for personal computers.

cards.headline: Blue micromoon rises this weekend
cards.teaser: A rare blue micromoon, the second full moon of May, appears in the night sky this weekend.
cards.body:
A blue micromoon is a rare celestial event occurring this weekend. Despite its name, the phenomenon isn't actually blue or particularly small. A blue moon refers to the second full moon appearing in a single calendar month, while a micromoon happens when the moon reaches its farthest point from Earth in its orbit.

This combination of events is uncommon, making it worth viewing. The best times and locations for observing the event are available for those planning to watch the night sky this weekend.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese technology investment firm plans to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data centers, marking a significant expansion of data infrastructure in Europe. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity.

This investment reflects the surging demand for data processing and storage as cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and digital services continue to grow globally.

cards.headline: James Bond game '007: First Light' becomes major sales hit
cards.teaser: The new James Bond video game sold heavily in its first 24 hours and received positive reviews for its cinematic approach.
cards.body:
The newly released James Bond game '007: First Light' has become a major sales success. Developed by IO Interactive, the stealth masters behind the Hitman franchise, the game follows a young Bond in his pre-00 days. Reviewers have praised its cinematic presentation and sophisticated design.

IO Interactive brought its signature style to the Bond universe, drawing on elements from its Hitman series—globetrotting missions, a besuited protagonist, and attention to corporate opulence and architecture. The game represents a significant achievement for the developer, which has long possessed the creative DNA to tackle a Bond game through its eye for spy craft and stylish presentation.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: A new wave of software updates addresses compatibility issues for original Switch games running on the Switch 2 console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released a new set of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on the Switch 2 console. The updates address issues that players have encountered when trying to play original Switch titles on the newer hardware.

The move continues Nintendo's effort to ensure a smooth transition for players moving from the original Switch to its successor. Backwards compatibility allows owners of the new console to continue playing their existing game libraries.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus could help restore habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: Scientists found a fungus species that may enable restoration of native British habitats overtaken by invasive moss.
cards.body:
A newly discovered species of fungus has raised hope that some native British habitats could be restored after being decimated by invasive moss. The fungus appears to affect the invasive moss in ways that could benefit native plant communities.

Researchers believe the discovery could provide a biological tool for habitat restoration efforts. Invasive moss has damaged numerous native ecosystems in Britain, displacing original vegetation and altering local environments.

hero.headline: Former NHL player Claude Lemieux dies at 60, brain donated for CTE research
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion, has died at age 60, with his family announcing that his brain will be donated to Boston University's CTE Center for research.

Police confirmed that Lemieux died by suicide. The former NHL star enjoyed a successful career spanning nearly two decades, winning Stanley Cup championships with three different teams.

Lemieux's family made the decision to donate his brain to the research center at Boston University, which studies chronic traumatic encephalopathy, a degenerative brain condition linked to repeated head trauma. The center has become a leading facility for examining the long-term effects of concussions and head injuries in athletes.

The NHL player's death adds to growing concerns about player safety and mental health in professional hockey. Lemieux played 1,215 regular season games during his NHL career, known for his physical style of play and postseason performances.

Lemieux won his first Stanley Cup with the Montreal Canadiens in 1986, followed by back-to-back championships with the New Jersey Devils in 1995 and 1996. He captured his fourth title with the Devils again in 2000. He was particularly known for his playoff success, earning the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP in 1995.

The donation of his brain to the CTE Center will allow researchers to examine whether Lemieux showed signs of the condition. CTE can only be definitively diagnosed after death through brain tissue examination. The condition has been found in numerous former professional athletes and has been associated with symptoms including depression, memory loss, and behavioral changes.

Boston University's CTE Center, founded by Dr. Ann McKee, has examined hundreds of brains from former athletes and military veterans. The research has helped establish links between repetitive head impacts in contact sports and long-term neurological damage.

Lemieux's death represents a significant loss to the hockey community. His career was marked by memorable playoff performances and a reputation as one of the game's most effective postseason players.

cards.headline: Victor Wembanyama leads Spurs past Thunder in Game 7 to reach NBA Finals
cards.teaser: San Antonio defeated the defending champions to advance to the NBA Finals against the Knicks.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs to a 111-103 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night. The win eliminated the defending champion Thunder and secured Wembanyama's first NBA Finals appearance.

The Spurs will now face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Champions League celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: Police detained hundreds as PSG fans fired flares and caused unrest following the Champions League final victory.
cards.body:
French authorities arrested hundreds of people after PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal sparked violent celebrations. Thousands of police officers were deployed across the country to control unruly crowds of fans.

During the celebrations, some supporters fired flares into the air. The widespread disturbances prompted a major law enforcement response as officers worked to restore order.

cards.headline: Brighton manager Dario Vidosic aims to honor late father in FA Cup final
cards.teaser: Vidosic will lead Brighton against Manchester City in the Women's FA Cup final.
cards.body:
Brighton manager Dario Vidosic will face Manchester City in Sunday's Women's FA Cup final at Wembley with his late father in his thoughts. Vidosic's father, Rado, who worked as the women's team's head of coaching, died from cancer four months ago.

Growing up in Brisbane, Vidosic cherished memories of staying up past his bedtime to watch Wembley finals with his father, then recreating great goals in the garden together the following day. Brighton are seeking their first major trophy in the final.

cards.headline: Gabriel's missed penalty gives PSG second consecutive Champions League title
cards.teaser: Arsenal defender Gabriel took his first penalty for the club in the shootout but his miss handed PSG the victory.
cards.body:
Gabriel's penalty miss proved decisive as Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League final shootout against Arsenal. The Arsenal defender, who volunteered to take the spot-kick, blazed his attempt over the bar in what became the decisive moment of the match.

PSG retained their Champions League crown, claiming back-to-back European titles. The victory sparked celebrations across France, with thousands of PSG supporters taking to the streets, though police had to manage unrest as crowds gathered to mark the win.

cards.headline: Arsenal to hold Premier League title parade day after Champions League loss
cards.teaser: The club will celebrate their league championship less than 24 hours after losing the European final.
cards.body:
Arsenal will celebrate their first Premier League title in 22 years with an open bus parade on Sunday, less than 24 hours after losing the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties in Budapest. Gabriel Magalhães's skied penalty in the shootout ended Arsenal's hopes of securing a domestic and European double.

Manager Mikel Arteta acknowledged the heartbreak of the defeat, particularly a missed penalty decision during extra time that he felt should have been awarded. However, Arteta emphasized the need to channel the disappointment constructively, urging the team to transform their pain "into fuel" for future competitions.

cards.headline: Darren Till wins bare-knuckle debut with knockout after early knockdown
cards.teaser: The former UFC fighter recovered from being dropped to finish Aaron Chalmers at BKFC 90.
cards.body:
Darren Till made a successful transition to bare-knuckle fighting at BKFC 90, defeating Aaron Chalmers with a knockout victory. The reality TV star dropped Till early in the fight, but the former MMA fighter recovered from the knockdown to turn the tide.

Till finished the fight with a vicious knockout, marking an impressive start to his bare-knuckle career following his time competing in mixed martial arts.

hero.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of Four Seasons Farewell Tour Due to Health Concerns
hero.body:
Music icon Frankie Valli has canceled the remaining dates of the Four Seasons farewell tour to focus on his health. The 92-year-old singer announced the decision on Saturday, ending what was planned as a final series of performances with his longtime band.

Valli apologized to fans in a statement, saying he was sorry to disappoint those who had planned to attend the canceled shows. The announcement comes partway through the 2026 tour, which was intended to be the group's final run of concerts.

The Four Seasons, formed in the 1960s, became one of the most successful American pop groups of the era with hits like "Sherry," "Big Girls Don't Cry," and "Walk Like a Man." Valli has continued performing for decades, maintaining an active touring schedule well into his 90s.

The singer did not provide specific details about the nature of his health concerns. The cancellation affects all remaining 2026 concert dates that had been scheduled as part of the farewell tour.

Fans who purchased tickets to the canceled performances will need to seek refunds through their point of purchase. The tour had been marketed as a final opportunity to see Valli and the Four Seasons perform their catalog of hits live.

Valli's career has spanned more than six decades, with the Four Seasons selling millions of records worldwide. The group's story was later adapted into the hit Broadway musical "Jersey Boys," which introduced their music to new generations of fans.

The decision to cancel comes as Valli prioritizes his health over completing the touring commitment. At 92, he had been among the oldest active touring performers in popular music.

cards.headline: Search Suspended for Man Believed to Be 'Alaskan Bush People' Star Matt Brown
cards.teaser: Authorities have suspended the search for a man believed to be reality TV personality Matt Brown after reports he took his own life.
cards.body:
The search for a man believed to be Matt Brown, a star of the reality series "Alaskan Bush People," has been suspended following reports that he took his own life. Brown's brother Bear confirmed that Matt was spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

Authorities had been searching the area where the man was last seen. The suspension of the search effort follows the reports about the circumstances of the disappearance. Brown appeared on the Discovery Channel series that followed his family living in remote Alaska.

cards.headline: Films Directed by YouTubers Top Box Office This Weekend
cards.teaser: The two highest-grossing films this weekend were both directed by filmmakers who started on YouTube.
cards.body:
"Backrooms" and "Obsession," the top two films at the box office this weekend, were both directed by creators who began their careers on YouTube. The success of the low-budget horror films has drawn attention from Hollywood executives and industry observers.

"Obsession" has overtaken "The Mandalorian and Grogu" at the box office, while "Backrooms" has become a word-of-mouth sensation. Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca compared the current moment to the edgy films of the 1970s, saying the success demonstrates a return to that era's creative energy.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt's Son Maddox Files to Drop Actor's Last Name
cards.teaser: Maddox Jolie-Pitt has filed to legally drop his father's surname.
cards.body:
Maddox, the son of Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, has filed paperwork to drop "Pitt" from his last name. The move comes amid the ongoing estrangement between Brad Pitt and some of his children with Jolie.

Brad Pitt was photographed in Paris with girlfriend Ines de Ramon following the news. Sources told media outlets that Pitt is hurt by his children dropping his last name and fears becoming permanently disconnected from them.

cards.headline: Chad Gable Unmasked as Original El Grande Americano at AAA Event
cards.teaser: WWE wrestler Chad Gable was revealed as the original El Grande Americano after losing a mask versus mask match.
cards.body:
Chad Gable lost his mask in a match at AAA Noche de Los Grandes on Saturday, officially revealing his identity as the original El Grande Americano. The mask versus mask bout has been described as a Match of the Year contender by wrestling media.

The event featured several high-profile matches, with results and highlights generating significant attention from wrestling fans. AAA, one of Mexico's premier wrestling promotions, held the show with participation from wrestlers from multiple organizations.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Second Cast Member in Consecutive Years for Using Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery will not appear on the upcoming season after social media posts surfaced.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed Vasana Montgomery from the cast after social media posts surfaced showing her using a racial slur. The decision marks the second consecutive year the reality dating series has dismissed a cast member for the same reason.

Montgomery will not appear when the show returns to Peacock on June 2. The removal came just two days before the season premiere, following the discovery of the posts on social media.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Death of Former Bandmate Liam Payne
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member discussed his memories of Payne in a recent interview.
cards.body:
Niall Horan opened up about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said he was with Payne in Argentina shortly before his death. He described experiencing both sadness and moments of laughter when remembering their shared experiences. Horan said the memories they created together sometimes make him laugh and smirk despite the loss.

hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
hero.body:
President Trump asked for several amendments to a nuclear agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to administration officials and sources briefed on the discussions.

Trump wants to finalize the deal soon but is seeking to strengthen several points that matter to him, particularly regarding Iran's nuclear material, two U.S. officials said. The president expects to complete the agreement despite the requested changes.

Trump's request has launched another round of negotiations between the parties that could last several more days. The back-and-forth comes as the administration works to extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The two sides reached a tentative agreement earlier in the week. If both Trump and Tehran ultimately approve the final terms, the emerging deal would mark a significant shift in U.S.-Iran relations. Details of a potential agreement include that the strait would reopen with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, while Iran would be able to freely sell oil. According to reports, negotiations would be held on curbing Iran's nuclear program. In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports.

Trump announced on Saturday that a peace deal "has been largely negotiated," after calls with a Pakistani mediator and Gulf allies. He wrote on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" were still being discussed and "will be announced shortly."

However, Iran's Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, reported that the strait of Hormuz would remain under Iranian control. The news agency stated that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

Pakistan's prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the U.S. and Iran "very soon." Pakistan's army chief, Syed Asim Munir, is a key figure in the negotiations.

The amendments focus on specific provisions related to Iran's nuclear program. Trump's decision to request modifications indicates his personal involvement in the final stages of the diplomatic process.

The agreement remains unsigned as the administration works to address Trump's concerns about nuclear material provisions and other key elements. Trump has said he would only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," adding that if an agreement was not reached, the U.S. would begin striking Iran again.

The negotiations have sparked criticism from Republican hawks who have spent years calling for military action against Iran and opposing the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated during the Obama administration.

cards.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch significant attacks within the next two days based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a major Russian attack expected within the next 48 hours, based on intelligence assessments from the U.S. and European allies. He anticipates the offensive will occur at night and involve significant Russian military forces.

The warning reflects ongoing concerns about Russian military operations against Ukraine and the coordination between Zelensky's government and Western intelligence partners in monitoring potential threats.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department asked a federal judge to step down from a lawsuit against Georgia election officials after she attended an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department filed a request on Friday asking a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials. The motion argues that the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial.

The filing was submitted to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia. The Justice Department contends that the judge's participation in the Willis event creates an appearance of bias that warrants her removal from the case.

cards.headline: UN blacklists Israeli and Russian forces for sexual violence during conflict
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces to its annual list documenting sexual violence during conflict, including allegations of rape against detained Palestinians.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israeli and Russian security forces for the first time to its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict. The report released Friday includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians by Israeli forces.

The U.N. report lists 77 government and non-government parties in countries credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other forms of sexual violence during armed conflict. The addition of Israeli and Russian forces marks the first time either has appeared on the list.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor steps down from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening President Trump has left the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case, according to a recent court filing. Comey faces charges for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells.

A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday stated that Matthew, the original prosecutor, would no longer be handling the case. The filing did not provide a reason for the change in legal representation.

cards.headline: Detainees sue over conditions at Texas ICE facility
cards.teaser: Immigrant detainees filed a lawsuit accusing the federal government of inhumane abuse and treatment at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement alleging severe violations of human and constitutional rights at Camp East Montana, the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees are listed as plaintiffs representing all current and future civil detainees at the El Paso facility.

The complaint documents multiple allegations including abhorrent medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, indiscriminate solitary confinement, inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations filed the suit on behalf of those held at the facility.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion fund for legal targets
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to review President Trump's $1.8 billion fund designed to compensate people he says were victims of political prosecution.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service to examine the $1.8 billion settlement. The review was triggered by a third-party motion claiming the settlement agreement is "a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court."

The original lawsuit, brought by Trump and his sons, stems from the unauthorized leak of their personal and business tax returns by a former IRS contractor. The judge's decision to revisit the case allows for investigation into whether the anti-weaponization fund settlement was negotiated improperly.
